body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application in view of the foregoing amendments and the reasons that follow.
Claims 1 and 26 have been amended. Claim 29 is new. Claims 10-12 have been
canceled. No new matter has been added. These amendments are made without prejudice or disclaimer.
After amending the claims as set forth above, claims 1-9 and 21-29 remain pending in this application. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of these claims.

Applicant appreciates the indication that claims 26-27 are allowable. With this reply, claim 26 has been rewritten in independent form including features corresponding to those of independent claim 1 and intervening claims 3, 4, and 25. Claim 27 depends from claim 26 Accordingly, Applicant submits that claims 26 and 27 are in condition for allowance.

Applicant appreciates the courtesies extended to Applicant's representative during the interview on August 15, 2024, by Examiner Pruitt. During the interview, an amendment specifying that the second end of the pendulum arm configured to rotate freely "and without restraints on motion between two end stops" was discussed, as reflected in the PTO-issued interview summary dated August 20, 2024. The PTO's interview summary generally reflects certain topics discussed during the interview, although Applicant does not concede to the propriety of the assertions concerning the teachings of the proposed combination of prior art. Applicant appreciates Examiner Pruitt's indication that the proposed amendment appears to be

supported by the Specification. Examiner Pruitt indicated that it does not appear that the cited references disclose, teach, or suggest methods in which the second end of a pendulum is allowed to rotate freely while the rotor blades are rotating, but that further consideration would be required. New claim 29, presented herewith, recites a method including these features. No agreement was reached as to the ultimate allowability of the claims.

Claims 1-3, 5-9, and 28 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over EP 2,357,356 ("Katz") in view of JP 2009/103147 ("Ide"). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
Amended claim 1 recites, with emphasis added:
1. A tunable mass damper assembly attachable to a rotor blade
configured to rotate about a rotor axis, the tunable mass damper assembly
comprising:

a base configured to be attached to the rotor blade; and a pendulum mass structure comprising: a first end rotatably coupled to the base about a pivot axis substantially perpendicular to a plane containing the rotor axis; a second end configured to rotate freely and without restraints on motion between two end stops about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade about the rotor axis, wherein when the base is attached to the rotor blade, the pendulum
mass structure is coupled to the rotor blade only via the first end,
the pendulum mass structure being configured to reduce vibratory forces of the rotor blade induced by a rotation of the rotor blade
about the rotor axis, and
an entirety of the pendulum mass structure being configured to be contained within and enclosed by the rotor blade.

The combination of Katz and Ide does not disclose, teach, or suggest the combination of features recited in claim 1. For example, the combination of Katz and Ide does not disclose, teach, or suggest a tunable mass damper assembly including a pendulum mass structure with "a
second end configured to rotate freely and without restraints on motion between two end stops about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade about the rotor axis."
The Office Action alleges on pages 2-3 that "Katz implicitly discloses wherein the

second end is configured to rotate freely since the mass requires additional elements, e.g. springs or centrifugal forces, to hold mass in the neutral position which implicitly discloses that without these additional elements the mass would move to a non-neutral position, e.g. due to gravity." As noted in the Interview Summary, "rotate freely" was interpreted by the Office to mean "not prevented from rotating when acted upon by a force." Without acquiescing to the propriety of this interpretation, claim 1 has been amended to recite that the second end of the pendulum mass structure is "configured to rotate freely and without restraints on motion between two end stops" (emphasis added). As discussed during the interview, the springs or actuator of Katz restrain the rotation of the lever arms such that a second end of the lever arm is not "configured to rotate freely and without restraints on motion between two end stops," as recited in amended claim 1.
The Office Action further alleges on page 5 that Ide teaches "the pendulum mass

structure being free to rotate about a pivot point at the first end when not being actuated (Par 0035)." Paragraph [0035] of Ide states that "in the stepping motor 3 ... the output shaft 4 becomes free to rotate when the power is turned off." However, Ide does not disclose, teach, or suggest that the power to the stepping motor 3 is actually turned off such that a second end of a pendulum mass structure is "configured to rotate . .. in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade." Paragraph [0035] continues: "when the power is supplied, the arm 11 sets the arm 11 to the set angle," and "The arm 11 swings about the position of the axis C in a rotation plane parallel to the direction orthogonal to the axis of the output shaft 4 with the amplitude determined by the control unit 8." Thus, Ide does not suggest that power is not supplied to the stepping motor 3 when the damper is in use, such that the arm 11 would rotate "in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade."

Further, even assuming arguendo that Ide teaches that the damper could be used without activating the stepping motor 3, Ide does not disclose that the arm is configured to rotate "without restraints on motion between two end stops." Stepping (or stepper) motors may include permanent magnets that produce a detent torque when unpowered, which resists the rotation of the motor shaft. Although Ide discloses that "the output shaft 4 becomes free to rotate when the power is turned off," Ide does not disclose that the output shaft 4 is free to rotate "without restraints on motion between two end stops," as recited in amended claim 1. The Interview Summary indicates that "rotat[ing] freely" was interpreted as "not prevented from rotating when acted upon by a force." Further, even if the output shaft 4 may not be "prevented from rotating when acted upon by a force" when the stepping motor 3 is unpowered, Ide does not disclose that the arm 11 is free to rotate "without restraints on motion" such as a detent torque of the stepping motor 3.
For at least these reasons, amended claim 1 is allowable over the combination of Katz and Ide.
Claims 2, 3, 5-9, and 28 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein.
Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of Ide in further view of U.S. Patent No. 5,639,214 ("Guimbal").

Claim 4 depends from claim 1. Guimbal does not remedy the deficiencies of Katz and Ide discussed above with respect to claim 1. Accordingly, claim 1 and its dependent claim, claim 4, are allowable over the combination of Katz, Ide, and Guimbal.
Claims 21-24 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of Ide in further view of U.S. Patent No. 2,426,130 ("Wald").

Claims 21-24 depend from claim 1. Wald does not remedy the deficiencies of Katz and Ide discussed above with respect to claim 1. Accordingly, claim 1 and its dependent claims, claims 12-24, are allowable over the combination of Katz, Ide, and Wald.
Claim 25 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of Ide in further view of Guimbal in even further view of Wald.

Claim 25 depends from claim 1. As discussed above, Guimbal and Wald do not remedy the deficiencies of Katz and Ide discussed above with respect to claim 1. Accordingly, claim 1 and its dependent claim, claim 25, are allowable over the combination of Katz, Ide, Guimbal, and Wald.

To the extent a requirement for restriction and/or election of species was made final in this application, Applicant asserts that all pending claims other than those identified as withdrawn, are either generic or read on the elected invention and/or species. Applicant intends for this Reply to be fully responsive to the outstanding Office Action.
Applicant believes that the application is in condition for allowance. Favorable
reconsideration is respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned by telephone if it is felt that a telephone interview would advance prosecution.
Respectfully submitted,
